observations: The drain is the one observable difference between TryReadMore and its twin ReadMore: TryReadMore writes *drop_size unconditionally (the mov at 0x5f029cd runs before the size test at 0x5f029d1), while ReadMore's drain only writes *drop_size when the buffer is non-empty (upstream log_reader.cc:838-855). The case ledger pins this with empty-drain rows (drop_size becomes 0 even when drop_size_in was 999).

The eof path's return value is the ORIGINAL eof_ value (r12d = 1), not the callee's: UnmarkEOFInternal is void and FragmentBufferedReader::UnmarkEOF returns whatever al holds on its early-return path. The caller checks read_error_ after the call, never the return value -- so a foreign UnmarkEOF override that does nothing still makes TryReadMore return true with eof_ still set, and the caller (TryReadFragment) is the one that detects no progress.

The read path's ReportDrop(kBlockSize, status) is unconditional on error, even with 0 bytes read -- unlike UnmarkEOFInternal, which reports ReportDrop(added) only when added > 0. The two error arms are easy to confuse; the case ledger and tests pin both separately (a read-path error with 0 bytes still reports 32768; a refill error with 0 bytes reports nothing).

The UnmarkEOFInternal memmove guards are defensive in practice: in every reachable state buffer_.data() == backing_store_ + consumed (the tail was consumed from the buffer by remove_prefix) and the Read result lands exactly at the scratch offset (SequentialFileReader::Read always returns scratch, per #5992). The model pins both guards with synthetic states (foreign buffer_offset, foreign data_offset) so the branches are covered, and records them as synthetic in the case ledger.

FragmentBufferedReader::UnmarkEOF has NO eof_offset_ == 0 early return, unlike the base Reader::UnmarkEOF (upstream log_reader.cc:633-651). The base version is not present as a standalone function in node #115 (no FDE for it; the gap 0x5f01899..0x5f018d0 holds only the UnmarkEOF FDE's stack-check epilogue and int3 padding) -- its callers use the virtual slot, which for FragmentBufferedReader resolves to 0x5f01880.
The TEST_SYNC_POINT_CALLBACK hooks (TryReadMore FirstEOF, ReadMore AfterReadFile) are test-only and compiled out of the node #115 binary -- neither FDE contains such a call.
